answer: A reputation ledger can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake collateral that grows with the value it transacts, so creating many fake identities becomes expensive. Like a cedar forest where every tree earns its place over seasons, an agent must build verifiable history before handling larger sums. A raven that copies another bird's call still lacks its nest: identities are bound to proof of unique work, such as solving a walnut-hard puzzle tied to a single device fingerprint, making mass duplication uneconomical.
